prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Scottish National Party Manifesto 1997 — Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- “Yes We Can”: Scotland is wealthy, pays more to London than it receives, and can fund better services through independence.
- Independence is the means to deliver jobs, social justice, strong public services and a modern European democracy.

Path to independence
- A majority of SNP MPs would trigger negotiations with the UK and EU, lasting 6–12 months, followed by a single-question referendum on the settlement; then elections.
- EU membership would continue; open borders with England; pensions/investments protected by EU rules.
- Full citizenship and residence rights for all current residents.

Constitution and governance
- Written constitution and Bill of Rights, including social rights (health, housing, education, decent work).
- Unicameral Parliament elected by proportional representation; vote from age 16; public petitions; strong committees.
- Reform the monarchy’s role and funding; abolish unelected influence (no House of Lords role).
- Local government entrenched in the constitution; PR for councils.

Economy, tax and jobs
- Aim for full employment: 100,000 extra jobs; national apprenticeship scheme.
- Business tax cuts over four years: corporation tax 33p→30p; small companies 23p→18p; abolish Class IV NICs; reformed business rates.
- Growth agenda: export unit, R&D fund, tourism promotion, defence diversification.
- Fair personal taxation: introduce 15p starter rate; widen basic rate band; remove NI ceiling for higher earners; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%.
- Adopt EU Social Chapter; introduce a minimum wage (half median male earnings); charter for trade union rights.

Social justice and health
- Increase child benefit; restore benefits for 16–17s.
- Pensioner package: +£3/£5 per week, Cold Climate Allowance, remove standing charges for utilities, end means-testing for residential care.
- NHS: end internal market; reintegrate dentistry; +£35m p.a.; national/local health commissions; audit and prevention focus; ban tobacco advertising and raise tobacco duty.

Law, order and consumer protection
- “Zero tolerance” for community crime; bolster Procurator Fiscal service; develop alternatives to prison and rehabilitation; national vehicle register; total handgun ban; strengthen food safety via an independent Food & Consumer Health Agency.

Education, housing, local services and culture
- Hire 700 teachers; repair schools; classroom ICT and universal school internet.
- Free nursery education for all 3–4-year-olds; restore student grants; expand training; support Gaelic/Scots and community faith studies.
- Housing: transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government; build 20,000 affordable homes; renovate substandard stock; protect new/improved stock from discounted Right to Buy; abolish water quangos.
- Broadcasting: create a Scottish Broadcasting Corporation; support film via “Scottish Screen”; launch “Scot-Lot” lottery (no scratch cards).

Rural, sectoral and environment
- Abolish feudal tenure; Land Commission; transparent land register; local control of shore/seabed.
- Agriculture: BSE traceability, CAP reform, rural diversification fund; strengthen fisheries via Regional Councils, conservation, processing support.
- Forestry: double woodland in 25 years; new National Forest Enterprise Board.
- Environment: strengthen SEPA; national targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; shift to decommissioning/renewables; phase out nuclear power; invest in renewables and conservation; ensure fair gas network access.

Transport and telecoms
- Integrate transport; bring Scottish Railtrack assets into public ownership; electrify key lines; integrate bus/rail.
- Remove Skye Bridge tolls (move to shadow tolls, then public ownership); support ferries; adjust/abolish Air Passenger Duty in H&I; improve air links.
- Expand telecoms competition and rural connectivity; back distance learning and internet adoption.

Europe, world and defence
- Full EU membership with voting rights, more MEPs, and rotating presidency.
- Targeted diplomatic network; join UN, Commonwealth, Council of Europe; British Isles association.
- Scottish Defence Forces (army, navy, air force); remove Trident; phased withdrawal from NATO due to nuclear stance; peacekeeping college; defence diversification.

Finances
- Four-year, fully costed budget; claim of large relative fiscal surplus versus UK; inherit ~£38bn debt, with £6.6bn repayment in first four years.
- Redirect spending from Trident to services; fund tax cuts, investment, and social programmes while reducing debt.

TEXT_E:
Labour Party Manifesto 1997 – summary (under 500 words)

Vision and approach
- New Labour offers a modern, pragmatic centre-left “what counts is what works” programme for national renewal: for the many, not the few; ending old left/right dogmas; rebuilding trust through specific, measurable pledges.
- Ten core commitments: prioritize education; no rise in basic/top income tax; economic stability with low inflation; 250,000 young unemployed into work; rebuild the NHS and cut bureaucracy; be tough on crime and its causes (including halving juvenile case times); strengthen families and modernize welfare; safeguard the environment with integrated transport; clean up politics and decentralize power; lead and reform in Europe.

Economy, tax and work
- Stability first: tight inflation target; reform Bank of England for credible, depoliticized monetary policy; “golden rule” (borrow only to invest); stick to existing spending totals for 2 years; save to invest.
- No increase in basic/top income tax rates; long‑term goal of a 10p starting rate; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; fair, pro‑work tax/benefit reform.
- Fund a welfare‑to‑work programme via a one‑off windfall levy on privatized utilities.
- Back business: tougher competition law; fix and focus the Private Finance Initiative; Regional Development Agencies; support small firms (cut red tape, tackle late payment); science/technology and green industries push.
- Modern labour market: sensibly set National Minimum Wage via Low Pay Commission; union recognition where workers vote for it; support EU Social Chapter focused on employability.

Education and skills (number one priority)
- Cut infant class sizes to 30 or under by ending assisted places; universal nursery places for 4‑year‑olds.
- Drive up standards: literacy/numeracy targets, setting by ability, “fresh start” for failing schools; Education Action Zones; ICT National Grid for Learning; wire schools free.
- Support and accountability: General Teaching Council; tougher teacher training/induction; stronger heads.
- Lifelong learning: University for Industry; Individual Learning Accounts; income‑related graduate repayments.

Welfare to work and families
- 250,000 under‑25s off benefit into real jobs/training/education; help long‑term unemployed; tailored “Employment Zones”; clamp down on fraud.
- National childcare strategy; basic rights on working time, holidays, unpaid parental leave; retain and uprate Child Benefit.

NHS and public health
- End the internal market; shift money from admin to care; treat 100,000 extra patients as a first step; end waits for cancer surgery.
- Primary care‑led commissioning in groups; multi‑year service agreements; measure outcomes; raise NHS spending in real terms annually.
- Ban tobacco advertising; independent Food Standards Agency; promote telemedicine.

Crime and justice
- Tough on crime and causes: halve time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders; final warning system; Youth Offender Teams.
- Decentralize CPS; sentencing guidelines and transparency; tackle disorder, stalking, domestic violence; new offences for racial harassment; anti‑drugs coordinator; free vote to ban all handguns; better support for victims.

Housing, pensions, care
- Help homeowners (consumer protection, tackle gazumping); reinvest council house receipts to build/repair homes; license HMOs; introduce commonhold; restore duty to house priority homeless.
- Retain basic state pension (price‑linked); promote secure second “stakeholder” pensions; retain SERPS option; carers’ rights; Royal Commission on long‑term care.

Environment, transport, rural, culture
- Every department “green”; integrated transport: stronger rail regulation and a new rail authority; public/private partnership for London Underground; roads review; cleaner vehicles; protect rural services and the Post Office; reform CAP; wider countryside access and wildlife protection.
- Arts/sport: create NESTA for young talent; protect school playing fields; back England’s 2006 World Cup bid; reform the Lottery with a not‑for‑profit operator.

Clean politics and constitution
- End hereditary peers’ voting rights; transparent party funding, ban foreign donations; Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the ECHR.
- Devolution by referendum: Scottish Parliament; Welsh Assembly; London mayor/strategic authority; regional chambers and possible elected assemblies; modernize Commons; empower and make local government accountable (best value).

Europe, foreign policy, defence, development
- Lead EU reform (single market, enlargement, CAP/CFP change, openness); sign Social Chapter; EMU decision by economic test and referendum.
- Defence rooted in NATO; strategic review; retain Trident; pursue arms control and ban landmines; UN and Commonwealth reform and engagement; new International Development department, move toward UN 0.7% aid target; human rights and ICC; cut CO2 by 20% by 2010.

Five election pledges
- Smaller infant classes; fast‑track persistent young offenders; cut NHS waiting lists (100,000 extra treated via £100m from red tape); 250,000 under‑25s into work (funded by windfall levy); no rise in income tax rates, cut VAT on heating to 5%, keep inflation/interest rates low.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_E aligns more closely with this profile.
